goal: Establish open scholarly knowledge graph succeeding MAG
dataset: OpenAlex (Crossref, PubMed, ROR, DOAJ, institutional repositories)
method: Automated harvesting, concept/topic classification, persistent entity linking
evaluation: Entity coverage, completeness audits against Crossref and MAG
findings: Maps 250M+ works, 100M+ authors, 100K+ institutions with ROR integration
limitation: Automated entity resolution introduces occasional author split/merge noise

citation: Ferreira et al. (2012) [ACM SIGMOD Record 41(2):15-26 / DOI:10.1145/2350036.2350040]
goal: Systematic survey of automatic author name disambiguation (AND) methods in digital libraries
method: Taxonomy of grouping vs classification methods; heuristic vs machine learning
findings: Co-authorship networks and institutional affiliations provide the strongest disambiguation signals
limitation: High error rate on rare/emerging authors with zero collaboration history

goal: Model collaboration intensity and topological structure in scientific networks
method: Weighted bipartite projection; shortest path lengths, clustering transitivity
evaluation: Clustering coefficients, degree distributions, characteristic path lengths
findings: Introduced standard collaboration weighting w(u,v) = sum 1/(n-1) to penalize massive consortium papers
limitation: Homogeneous pairwise model ignores topic semantics, affiliations, and venue prestige

goal: Construct large-scale discovery dataset for CS research (D3)
dataset: DBLP, Semantic Scholar (S2ORC), Computer Science Ontology (CSO)
method: Extracted full-text metadata (abstracts, affiliations, citations) mapped to CSO concepts
evaluation: Corpus growth rates, citation distributions, topic trend analysis
findings: Built unified CS dataset of 6M+ papers; demonstrated growth of multi-authorship
limitation: License ambiguity (CC BY vs CC BY-NC); hierarchical CSO tags cause substantial domain drift

goal: Survey of graph database models and expressiveness
method: Comparative analysis of data representation, query languages, and traversal performance
findings: Labeled Property Graphs (LPG) natively represent edge attributes without RDF reification overhead
limitation: Lacks standardized formal declarative query syntax across legacy engines (resolved by openCypher/GQL)

citation: Visser et al. (2021) [Quantitative Science Studies 2(1):20-40 / DOI:10.1162/qss_a_00112]
goal: Large-scale comparative analysis of bibliographic data sources
dataset: Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, Crossref, Microsoft Academic
method: Cross-database coverage matching, publication types, citation completeness
evaluation: Overlap percentages, citation correlation, field coverage
findings: Microsoft Academic/OpenAlex provided superior coverage of computer science proceedings and preprints
limitation: Metadata completeness for affiliations in older records lags behind curated databases

goal: Resolve disconnected community anomaly in modularity maximization
method: Leiden algorithm (refinement of Louvain with guaranteed connectedness)
evaluation: Modularity Q, CPM (Constant Potts Model), runtime scalability
findings: Guarantees well-connected communities and eliminates Louvain's arbitrarily disconnected clusters
limitation: Modularity optimization on disconnected graphs trivially yields near-1.0 Q scores

goal: Inductive representation learning on large graphs
evaluation: Micro-averaged F1, Link Prediction MRR, node classification accuracy
findings: Enables inductive embedding of unseen nodes without re-training full graph
limitation: Full multi-relational heterogeneity requires adaptation (e.g. RGCN/HGT)

goal: Representation learning on heterogeneous information networks
evaluation: Link prediction AUC, multi-class node classification
findings: Outperformed homogeneous random walks (DeepWalk/Node2Vec) by preserving relation semantics
limitation: Requires manual pre-specification of meta-paths (e.g. Author-Paper-Author)

goal: Collaborator recommendation using multi-attribute graph models
method: Hybrid link prediction combining topological features and LDA topic vectors
findings: Combining topological proximity with thematic topic overlap significantly boosts recommendation precision
limitation: Evaluated on static cross-validation; susceptible to temporal data leakage
